source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Wait for medical confirmation of physical injury before reporting because suspicion alone is not enough to contact protective services.","B":"Keep suspected financial exploitation or neglect within the family unless the older adult specifically requests a formal report.","C":"Recognize physical, emotional, sexual, financial, and neglect-related abuse and follow current state law and policy for reporting to APS or emergency/law-enforcement services as appropriate.","D":"Limit reporting to licensed clinicians because family members and community workers cannot contact Adult Protective Services about suspected maltreatment."}}
source_row.rationale: Elder maltreatment can include physical, emotional, sexual, financial, and neglect-related harm. ACL identifies Adult Protective Services as a principal response agency and directs emergency action when immediate danger exists. For nursing practice, the exact mandatory-reporting duty must follow current state law and organizational policy; therefore option C is accurate without falsely imposing one universal reporting procedure on every jurisdiction.
source_row.source_detail: HHS Administration for Community Living — What If I Suspect Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation?: Adult Protective Services is the principal public agency responding to reports of abuse/neglect/exploitation of vulnerable adults; use emergency/law-enforcement channels when immediate danger exists. Reporting duties vary by state law. ACL page modified 2026-03-18; current federal elder-justice guidance rechecked 2026-08-15. Mandatory-reporting duties must be applied under current jurisdiction law/policy. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Psychosocial Integrity: cultural practices/beliefs, abuse/neglect reporting, coping, mental-health symptoms and therapeutic adaptation activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
